- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% of recent mean to avoid undershoot.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 3–5% in next 3–5 days to reflect mean reversion.
- If sentiment is positive and price is falling, model may underestimate support; add 1–3% buffer to lower end of forecast range.
- Model frequently underestimates true price decline in early 30-day horizon; apply 1–2% upward bias to forecast if sentiment is neutral or mildly negative.
- When sentiment is volatile or mixed, model tends to overfit recent trends; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values before projecting.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion after a 10–15 day run, model often fails to recognize it; reduce forecast slope by 20–30% in next 5–7 days.
